clue.text: I: speak

definitions.note: I is the standard map abbreviation for island, so it stands for a Hebridean isle here

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue is a colon
to speak is to say

explanation.surface: Someone announcing that it is their turn to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed colon is not just punctuation: it is a piece of wordplay, read as its name. Throughout this puzzle a bare 'I' stands for an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonsay is a small island of the Inner Hebrides, and I abbreviates island.

clue.text: I, first of ideas yet to be hatched?

definitions.note: I is the standard map abbreviation for island

indicators.note: yet means still, so the letter is still sitting within the egg rather than out of it

parts.note: something to be hatched is an egg

indicators.note: first of picks out only the opening letter of the word ideas

explanation.surface: Someone describing their half-formed thoughts as eggs not yet hatched.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: an idea yet to be hatched is one still sitting in its egg. 'yet' places the letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Eigg is one of the Small Isles of the Inner Hebrides; I abbreviates island.

clue.text: Being hospitable finally, US city welcoming bird

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the word hospitable
welcoming means taking a guest in, so the city's letters enclose the bird

parts.note: NY is short for New York
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: An American city praised for welcoming a bird, being hospitable at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb tying the clue together, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is a thing with distinct existence, a being.

clue.text: Shrewd to fix duel in competition

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for a competition

parts.note: a cup is a sporting competition, such as the FA Cup

indicators.note: to fix suggests rigging or rearranging, so the letters of duel are reordered

explanation.surface: A cunning plan to rig a duel within a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fix' looks like the plan of the shrewd schemer, but it is the anagram signal; 'competition' is a trophy contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well informed and knowing, as the idiom has it, makes one shrewd.

clue.text: Cry is directed at a nymph

parts.note: to cry out is to call
directed at something means sent to it

explanation.surface: A shout aimed at a woodland spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Callisto was a nymph of Artemis turned into a bear.

clue.text: Bar selling rum seems familiar

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A pub selling rum is a familiar sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink being sold, but it is the adjective for strange, signalling an anagram of BAR SELLING.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something that strikes a chord or prompts a memory seems familiar.

clue.text: Seafood with not as much hesitation thrown up

indicators.note: in a down entry thrown up means written from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: not as much means less
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Seafood that, eaten with less hesitation, comes back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown up' turns LESSUM around to read upwards, a nod to the seafood's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is an edible bivalve shellfish, a type of seafood.

clue.text: Minus I, lake is imaginary

parts.note: minus means without, which is not having
I stands for an island in this puzzle, here the Hebridean isle of Iona
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Without I, a lake becomes imaginary.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'I' is not a letter to remove: it is an island again, IONA, home of St Columba's abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means existing only as an idea, hypothetical or imaginary.

clue.text: I'm going mad, ie unhinged to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone declaring they are losing their mind, or rather unhinged to a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell, said when one is leaving.

clue.text: Flag's back alongside issue number

indicators.note: alongside places the flag's letter next to the offspring word

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son

indicators.note: back means the rear end of the word flag, its final letter

explanation.surface: A flag is back next to an issue number, like a magazine edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag's' reads as 'Flag is'. 'number' looks like part of 'issue number' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a piece of music performed, such as a song.

clue.text: Record first put on tape a non-starter for visionary

indicators.note: put on means placed after, so the record and first follow the tape
a non-starter means losing the opening letter of the word for tape

parts.note: a video is a recording tape
a log is a record, like a ship's log
1ST is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A dreamer's failed project to put a first record onto tape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a non-starter' means the tape word loses its first letter; 'put on' says the record and the abbreviation for first follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideologist is a theorist or dreamer of ideas, a visionary.

clue.text: Very contrary, kill bird

indicators.note: contrary means turned the other way, so the word for very reads backwards

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
a kill is prey, the animal caught by a hunter

explanation.surface: A very contrary person kills a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating hawk, a bird of prey.

clue.text: New Orleans, and a case of blue sound

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged
case of means the outer shell of the word blue, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: New Orleans, home of jazz and a blues sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of the city's name but is the anagram signal. ORLEANS, A and BE (the case of 'blue') are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is a sensible, reasonable one: a synonym.

clue.text: Rocky I, fit

parts.note: I stands for an island in this puzzle, here Unst in Shetland
fit means capable or able

explanation.surface: A boxer like Rocky declaring himself fit.
explanation.walkthrough: UNST is the most northerly inhabited Shetland island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky means shaky, wobbly, unsteady.

clue.text: Tiny gap unknown in fractures close to ankle

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the word for fractures

parts.note: snaps means breaks or fractures
Y is an unknown in algebra

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word ankle

explanation.surface: A medical note about a small gap in fractures near the ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: A synapse is the minute junction between nerve cells across which impulses pass.

clue.text: Across middle, regular parts lost among rocks

indicators.note: among puts the kept letters inside the word for rocks

parts.note: rocks means sways to and fro

indicators.note: regular parts lost says every other letter of middle is dropped, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A geology note about rock with regular sections missing across its middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular parts lost' keeps the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'middle'. 'Across', in a crossword, looks like a direction label but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going sideways means moving crosswise, laterally.

clue.text: I must secure home, in truth

indicators.note: must secure means holding something within, so the island's letters enclose the home

parts.note: I stands for an island in this puzzle, here Hoy in Orkney
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to make their house safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoy is an island in Orkney, off Scotland's north coast; 'must secure' says it holds the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty is truthfulness, the quality of being truthful.

clue.text: Body parts from the wielder of a hammer and hatchets

parts.note: Thor, the Norse god of thunder, wields the hammer Mjolnir
hatchets are small axes

explanation.surface: Body parts produced by someone with a hammer and hatchets, a gruesome scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoraxes are chests, the parts of the body between neck and abdomen.

clue.text: I, U and I deviate

definitions.note: I stands for an island, here one in Orkney

parts.note: you and I, with U as text shorthand for you, together make we
to deviate is to stray from a path

explanation.surface: A text-speak note about two people drifting apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' is text shorthand for 'you', so 'U and I' is WE.
explanation.definitionFit: Westray is one of the Orkney islands; I abbreviates island.

clue.text: Nothing to achieve on reflection in message — that's the whole thing

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for message

parts.note: a cable is a telegram message

indicators.note: on reflection means seen as in a mirror, so the letters read backwards
to means added onto, so nothing is attached after achieve

parts.note: to achieve something is to do it
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: On reflection, a message saying there is nothing to achieve is all there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns the achieve-plus-nothing pair, giving OOD; 'Cable' is an old word for a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole caboodle is an idiom for everything, every part included.

clue.text: Skilful commercial industry initially in decay

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: in places the initial inside the word for decay

parts.note: rot means decay

indicators.note: initially takes only the opening letter of the word industry

explanation.surface: A skilful advert about an industry in decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means dexterous, clever with the hands or mind.

clue.text: I am in debt, endlessly, as spineless

parts.note: I stands for an island in this puzzle, here Yell in Shetland

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the word for being in debt

parts.note: to be in debt is to owe

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they are endlessly in debt and feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am' reads as one phrase but 'I' is the island YELL, and 'am in debt' is OWE, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, lacking backbone.

clue.text: Haul up fish on line in river

indicators.note: on means placed above, so the fish sits on top of the line in a down entry
haul up means pull upwards, so in a down entry the fish's letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
a row is a line

explanation.surface: An angler pulling up a fish on a line in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue means one piece sits above another.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yarrow Water is a river in the Scottish Borders, famous in ballads.

clue.text: Main barrier takes a little time to split weaker bar that's damaged

indicators.note: to split means to break into, so the time letter goes inside
damaged means broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is a short abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A barrier delayed by having to break up a weak bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, not 'principal'. T splits the anagram of WEAKER BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakwater is a barrier built out into the sea to shelter a harbour from waves.

clue.text: Intend to be cruel

definitions.meaning: to intend something is to have it in mind as a purpose
unkind or nasty, as in a nasty trick

explanation.surface: Meaning to be cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to have in mind as purpose, and an unkind spiteful nature.

clue.text: I refuse

definitions.meaning: I stands for an island, here one of the Small Isles of the Inner Hebrides
refuse is rubbish, dirt or dung

explanation.definitionFit: Muck is one of the Small Isles, and muck also means dirt or rubbish.

clue.text: I, I kill

parts.note: I stands for an island, here the southernmost of the Inner Hebrides
to slay is to kill

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to murder.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'I' is the island, the second just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Islay is a Hebridean island famous for whisky; I abbreviates island.

clue.text: A very old revolutionary in America confesses

indicators.note: in puts the revolutionary inside the country abbreviation

parts.note: US is the United States
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: An aged revolutionary in America makes a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: To avouch is to affirm or acknowledge openly, to admit.
